findings.title: `Market.source_bar_stamping` accepts a plain `str`, unlike every other enum field in the module
findings.description:
`__post_init__` validates this field with `if self.source_bar_stamping not in SOURCE_BAR_STAMPINGS:`. Because `TimeMeaning` is a `StrEnum`, its members hash and compare equal to their string values (`str.__hash__`/`str.__eq__` precede `Enum`'s in the MRO), so `SOURCE_BAR_STAMPINGS` accepts the plain string `"period_start"`. The check therefore admits a value that is not a `TimeMeaning` and stores it verbatim on a canonical type.

This is inconsistent with the rest of the module: `continuity_kind` (`markets.py:102`), `SessionCalendarRef.session_mode` (`markets.py:64`), and every `adjustment_bases` element (`markets.py:165`) all go through `_require_instance`, which rejects a plain `str`. `source_bar_stamping` is the only enum field that does not.

The concrete risk is identity-based checks. `period_end.py:82` uses exactly this pattern (`if start.meaning is not TimeMeaning.PERIOD_START:`). A market built from untyped external metadata (the 140 adapter that populates `Market` from trading-data) can hold `"period_start"` instead of `TimeMeaning.PERIOD_START`; the canonical bytes are identical (both encode to `"period_start"`), so no golden vector catches it, but `market.source_bar_stamping is TimeMeaning.PERIOD_START` is `False` and an `is`-based consumer silently takes the wrong branch. The same looseness affects the lookups: `calendar_id_for("extended")` (`markets.py:106`) and `require_adjustment_basis("raw")` (`markets.py:115`) both succeed on a plain string.

Suggested fix: validate with `_require_instance(self.source_bar_stamping, TimeMeaning, "market.source_bar_stamping")` before the membership test, matching the other fields.

findings.title: Market normalization leaks raw `TypeError` instead of the documented `InvalidMarketError`
findings.description:
The slice design's data-flow contract states that invalid input "raises `InvalidMarketError` or `InvalidInstrumentError` naming the field", and the error hierarchy exists precisely so callers can catch `CoreModelError` at a boundary. Two paths in `Market.__post_init__` break that contract:

- `_normalize_calendars` calls `items = tuple(refs)` (`markets.py:144`) before any type check, so `Market(session_calendars=None)` or `Market(session_calendars=5)` raises `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable` instead of `InvalidMarketError` naming the field.
- `_normalize_bases` calls `items = frozenset(bases)` (`markets.py:161`) before validating element types, so an unhashable element such as `Market(adjustment_bases=[AdjustmentBasis.RAW, ["x"]])` raises `TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'`. The existing test (`test_markets.py`, "non-basis element") only covers a hashable `"raw2"`, which is why this path is not exercised.

The element-type check that does exist (`markets.py:165`) runs only after the set has been built, so it cannot catch this class of input. Concretely: validate the container type first (or wrap the iteration in a narrow `try`/`except TypeError` that re-raises `InvalidMarketError` naming the field), and validate each element's type before it is hashed.

findings.title: Dead constant `SIXTY_SECONDS_NS` in the uniformity test
findings.description: `SIXTY_SECONDS_NS = 60_000_000_000` is defined but never referenced; a grep across `tests/` finds only the definition line. The bar width is passed as `BarSpec.time(60)` at line 56 and the expected ends are written as full literals in `UNIFORM_ROWS`, so the constant is a leftover. Ruff does not flag unused module-level constants (only `F401` for imports and `F841` for locals), so it will silently persist. Removing it is the simplest fix.

findings.title: The uniformity test duplicates the fixture-instrument list instead of deriving from `ALL_INSTRUMENT_FIXTURES`
findings.description: `fixtures/instruments.py` defines `ALL_INSTRUMENT_FIXTURES` as the single list of fixture instruments, but `test_market_uniformity.py` builds a second, parallel list, `UNIFORM_ROWS`, repeating all five instruments. The slice design states the uniformity test is "parametrized over `ALL_INSTRUMENT_FIXTURES`". Because the two lists are independent, adding a sixth fixture instrument to `ALL_INSTRUMENT_FIXTURES` will not extend the uniformity coverage — and the uniformity test is precisely the guard that proves "one code path serves every market". Adding an assertion that the instruments in `UNIFORM_ROWS` are exactly `ALL_INSTRUMENT_FIXTURES` would make the drift impossible.

findings.title: `Market`'s declared field types contradict the documented "accepts any iterable" contract
findings.description: The fields are declared `session_calendars: tuple[SessionCalendarRef, ...]` and `adjustment_bases: frozenset[AdjustmentBasis]`, but the class docstring and the slice design both promise that these "accept any iterable", and `test_markets.py::test_generator_and_set_are_accepted` exercises a generator and a `set`. A caller following the documented contract and passing a list or generator is rejected by strict pyright, because the dataclass field annotation doubles as the constructor parameter type. Since `pyproject.toml` sets `typeCheckingMode = "strict"` and CI runs `uv run pyright`, real callers will hit this. Either narrow the documented promise to the declared types, or accept `Iterable[...]` at the boundary and convert it before construction.

findings.title: `test_canonical_golden.py` now exceeds the project's ~300-line file-size convention
findings.description: The file grew from roughly 275 to 360 lines with this change's nine market and instrument golden rows, crossing the AGENTS.md guideline of "Keep source files to ~300 lines". The slice's own task breakdown already identified this and named the remedy: "The natural split is the 102 rows into `test_canonical_golden_markets.py`." The split was not performed. Moving the new market and instrument rows into a dedicated golden module would restore the convention and keep the hand-derived-oracle rationale documented per file.
